claude.request:
Today's international headlines:
- Flight recorders recovered from Amazon cargo plane crash: Five people were killed and five others seriously injured when the Boeing 767-300 overshot the runway at Miami International Airport.
- Palestinian parents fear for children's lives at school as settler attacks grow: A headteacher in the occupied West Bank has installed new barbed wire fencing after three pupils were killed this year.
- Germany's far-right AfD says 'democracy demands' parties work with them after state election win: The far-right party is trying to form a government in the state after falling three seats short of a majority.
- Eiffel Tower shut by staff protest after female workers moved for religious visit: An investigation will be launched into the incident, which left female employees "humiliated", a union representative says.
- Ukraine's chief prosecutor resigns over call centre corruption scandal: In his resignation letter, Ruslan Kravchenko denied the allegations against him, saying he did not want his office "to be used as a tool in political confrontation".
- UK government expected to announce restrictions on trade with West Bank settlements: Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband is set to outline the proposals today, in a move which could prompt Israel to retaliate.
- Trump threatens to stop sale of Canadian Bombardier jets in US: The threat against one of Canada's largest companies comes amid an escalating trade war between the two neighbours.
- North Korea and Russia open first road bridge linking both countries: It comes as relations between both countries have strengthened since the start of the Ukraine war.
- Trial over alleged murders of Australian surfer brothers starts in Mexico: The bodies of Jake and Callum Robinson and their US friend were found with gunshot wounds to their heads.
- Thousands turn out in Serbia for funeral of  'Butcher of Bosnia' Ratko Mladić: Mladić was jailed for genocide during the 1990s Bosnian war and the EU warned Serbia not to glorify the convicted war criminal.
- Israeli strikes in southern Lebanese village kill 12: Lebanon says a recent Israeli escalation is jeopardising a US-brokered ceasefire meant to end the conflict between Israel and Hezbollah.
- Grindr to pay £26m to settle claims it allegedly shared users' HIV status: The long-running claim alleges Grindr breached UK privacy laws by sharing data with third parties.
